name: embater
description: Count columns or the spaces between them; compare Vitruvius with 31 temple records and save the illustrated reading. Also explore the orders, temple plans and architectural vocabulary.

study.finding: For six columns across, doubling five spaces gives eleven along the side. Compare the prescription with 31 Perseus records; two restorations are uncertain.

workshops.title: Count the spaces
workshops.summary: Choose which noun to double, compare 31 temple records, and save a source-backed illustrated reading. Two uncertain restorations can be included in the tally.

name: harmoniai
description: Pluck the fifteen strings of the Greek two-octave system, hear Cleonides' seven octave species, and run Bharata's two-vīṇā demonstration of the twenty-two śrutis.

study.finding: Cleonides' two descriptions of the octaves agree; on white keys his Dorian is today's Phrygian, and his Phrygian today's Dorian.

workshops.title: The same meetings, unequal lowerings
workshops.summary: The seven string meetings do not force equal steps. Inspect a pure-ratio counterexample, compare the two fifths by ear, and follow the source and tunable model.

name: haidao
description: Test Liu Hui’s sea-island recipe against two independent sightings. Read Classical Chinese beside a later printed witness, choose between two divisors, and explore uncertainty in the retreats.

study.finding: The pole-gap divisor passes the first sighting but misses the second by 4980/127 bu. Allowing ±2 bu in each retreat leaves no finite upper height bound.

name: rajju
description: Place Āpastamba’s four corner pegs with marked cords. Separate the grip from the stake, compare four procedures, and read Sanskrit beside original pages; explore circle and diagonal rules too.

study.finding: Holding at 15 makes a perpendicular; staking at 12 gives the prescribed ground. Staking both eastern grips changes area from 972 to 1080.

name: pnigeus
description: Read Hero’s Greek beside the source page. Compare a water-organ hemisphere, cylinder and cone; explore pressure, air reserve, pumping and Vitruvius’s Latin.

study.finding: In the 80 cm model, a 30% pressure drop loses 49.97 L of chamber space but supplies 54.72 ambient L. Halving radius divides space by eight.

name: sammu
description: Follow an Old Babylonian retuning procedure on nine strings. Retune by ear with isolated partials, hear overtones, learn Akkadian terms, and keep exact pitch histories from a Mesopotamian model.

study.finding: Seven retunings return the name while shifting every pitch in the 4/3–3/2 model; reversing the route restores the exact starting frequencies.

name: seked
description: Dissect a square frustum into nine pieces; keep the Moscow papyrus calculation separate from the modern proof. Read six Rhind slope exercises, compare face and corner sections, and inspect the printed sources.

study.finding: Separate nine solid pieces: 4,2,6 gives 56. Averaging the end areas gives 60; the midpoint estimate gives 54.

name: shiguzhai
description: Explore two Chinese bell studies: keep Shiguzhai’s observed pitch lists, then couple Piao-shi bending patterns and compare a bell-maker’s Chinese proportions with measured dimensions.

study.finding: The model strike changes a mixture of 1214.1/1486.8 Hz; two readings predict a mouth depth of 6 or 6.4 for a ridge length of ten.

name: pyknon
description: Translate Greek musical signs without changing the notes. Compare two alphabets and two table functions; hear ancient musical arguments through explicit modern models and read their printed evidence.

study.finding: Two copied shapes change two notes. Hold both tables’ mesai at a modern 330 Hz: iota becomes 330 or 440 Hz. Both printed functions remain.

workshops.title: One bridge. Four strings. · Ptolemy’s helikon
workshops.summary: Build Ptolemy’s four-string geometry and hear seven interval relations. Keep the end notes fixed, fit three targets by moving the inner strings, then transpose without erasing interval errors. Greek, Latin and whole printed evidence remain beside the experiment.

workshops.title: Keep the notes. Change the signs. · Alypius
workshops.summary: Translate a four-note practice line while keeping the paired lookup visible. A copied shape can change the note. Compare shared signs under two explicit pitch constraints, then read the Greek descriptions and whole 1895 pages.

workshops.title: Six tones and an octave · Sectio canonis
workshops.summary: Stack six 9:8 steps against modern equal octave divisions. Compare the exact ratios and synthetic tones, then read the Greek argument.

workshops.title: Equal lengths. Unequal notes. · Ptolemy
workshops.summary: Equal halves can pass a string test while the right-hand quarters fail. Change a disclosed mass profile, compare the modern vibration model and read Ptolemy’s examination.

workshops.title: Same matches. Different pitches. · Two vinas
workshops.summary: Keep the text’s successive pitch matches, change a disclosed modern tuning preparation, and compare the different pitches that still satisfy them.

workshops.title: Three middles. One interval. · Sectio canonis III & XVI
workshops.summary: Seventeen is halfway between sixteen and eighteen by addition, but 17/16 and 18/17 differ. Compare three middles, hear the halves, and inspect the whole-number premise of the Greek proof.

name: grama
description: Change the starting note, then lower Pa in the Nāṭyaśāstra’s two grāmas. Separate twenty-two counted intervals from assumed pitches; hear both models and read Sanskrit beside complete printed evidence.

study.finding: The same count change lowers Pa by 21.506 cents in a modern ratio example, or 54.545 in equal division. The count row alone leaves pitches undetermined.

name: zygon
description: Operate Archimedes’ balances, finite parabola bounds and floating bodies. Read the Greek and Latin conditions beside complete manuscript and printed sources.

study.finding: Eight midpoint bands balance exactly, while the sphere estimate remains high by πr³/96; equal moments do not make each volume exact.

workshops.title: It floats. Will it stay upright? · Archimedes’ floating solids
workshops.summary: Balance equal vertical forces, then see a tall, light solid turn farther over. Change density, find an oblique equilibrium, and read the Greek dry-base condition.

workshops.title: A third more · Archimedes’ parabola and its finite remainder
workshops.summary: Find one arm for every interior section, then test a proposed area against finite bounds. Reject wrong guesses, keep a close proposal’s layer-10 account distinct from the seven drawn refinements, and read the Greek/Latin proof qualification.

name: dioptra
description: Calibrate Hero’s distance counter by trial: keep its pointers and change the distance scale. Compare Frontinus’s Latin pipe names, circular openings and relative delivery; also measure water supply and tunnel routes.

study.finding: A completed twenty-turn trial changes the same fifteen dial divisions from 1,200 to 800 cubits, without moving either pointer.

workshops.title: Double the bore · Frontinus’s pipe gauges
workshops.summary: Compare opening area and maintained head. An opening four times the area can give the same model delivery at lower head; read Frontinus’s Latin qualification.

name: gonia
description: Draw an Ionic scroll with twelve compass centres. Test why meeting the eye does not make a tangent, read Vitruvius’s Latin, and inspect the printed guide and surviving stone. Explore fourteen more architectural experiments.

study.finding: Twelve compass arcs reach the eye but leave an 8.130102° turn. Aligning one tangent moves the next endpoint; the modern model is not an ancient drawing.

workshops.title: The arch and the pier: contact is not enough
workshops.summary: Fit every contact, then test whether the joints and bases can carry the shear. Compare finite friction, a repaired force path and a sliding base beside Vitruvius’s Latin and whole source pages.

workshops.title: The cut inside a column · Fluting
workshops.summary: Move a right-angle tool across Vitruvius’s Doric and Ionic hollows. Compare the tool fit and read the Latin beside Aristotle’s Greek word for fluting.

workshops.title: The curve inside the taper · Entasis
workshops.summary: Compare Penrose’s measured offsets with a straight taper. Enlarge the departure explicitly, inspect a station and read the surviving Latin without supplying its lost diagram.

workshops.title: Seven names, one uneven obol · Building accounts
workshops.summary: Balance a hundred-drachma entry, then move one obol between names. The total still fits while the edited allocation changes; locate the name in the Greek account.

workshops.title: A tower between two sources · Babylon
workshops.summary: Keep the sixth storey unknown, or supply a disclosed completion. Compare a tablet’s numerical scheme with calibrated stele measurements and inspect the carved stone.

workshops.title: The compass changes centre: draw an Ionic volute
workshops.summary: Choose twelve compass pins, retain wrong turns and inspect the tangent at every join. Read the Latin beside complete pages; keep the later guide separate from the surviving capital.

name: syngraphe
description: Fifteen feet includes the pillar. Read the Piraeus naval-storehouse programme in Greek, correct two plausible misreadings and compare measured drawings with whole printed pages.

study.finding: A thirty-foot total can still violate the first-segment clause. Inclusive Greek measurements constrain a drawing without completing a reconstruction.

workshops.title: A building in the words · Piraeus
workshops.summary: Correct an inclusive width, expose a wrong first segment inside a matching total and compare two modern grids under selected clauses. Read the Greek and the whole printed evidence.

name: stoicheia
description: Double a polygon’s sides, then change one root estimate: does Archimedes’ circle bound still have a proof? Read the Greek and Latin, inspect ten original pages and save the complete illustrated argument.

study.finding: A failed outer root estimate leaves its current perimeter bound intact, then breaks the next bisection’s proof. Exact fractions reveal why.

workshops.title: Two fits. One limit. · Euclid’s application of areas
workshops.summary: Find two area fits, meet at their maximum, then keep an impossible target while changing falling short to exceeding. Read the Greek and Latin condition beside whole pages; save exact work and certified bounds for irrational fits.

workshops.title: Euclid’s extra prime · IX.20 and the composite case
workshops.summary: Propose a prime divisor and check three separate conditions while the bounded search stays unresolved. Reject the unit and the whole composite sum, then read both Greek/Latin cases beside complete printed pages.

workshops.title: Six faces. Still not one of five. · Euclid’s solid corners
workshops.summary: Add a sixth triangle: the vertex goes flat. Compare two joined tetrahedra with uniform regular solids; equal faces can have different corners. Read the Greek and Latin, test the missing condition and keep a calibrated paper experiment.

workshops.title: Thousands agree. One can disagree. · Euclid V.5
workshops.summary: Search 4,761 multiplier pairs that agree, then find one exact disagreement. Read Euclid V.5 in Greek and Latin and distinguish finite agreement from the universal condition.

workshops.title: The point the motion cannot draw · Pappus
workshops.summary: Approach the end of synchronized motion, then finish exactly. The crossing becomes coincident lines; compare a separately added limit point with the Greek and Latin readings.

workshops.title: A line that will not fit · Euclid III.16
workshops.summary: Hide a ray’s crossing below the pixel scale, then inspect an exact positive deficit. Compare the tiny crossing with the tangent and read Euclid’s horn-angle argument.

workshops.title: Keep the safe side · Archimedes
workshops.summary: Change one root estimate in Archimedes’ polygon calculation. Track which perimeter bound remains justified and where its proof chain first breaks, beside Greek and Latin.

workshops.title: A common measure · Euclid X.2–3
workshops.summary: Repeat subtraction for a rational ratio and a square diagonal. Compare a finite common measure with a positive remainder, then read the distinct recurrence argument in Greek and Latin.

workshops.title: Make I.2 yourself · Construction desk
workshops.summary: Choose circles, lines and their crossings to construct Euclid I.2 yourself. Work with the restricted compass, inspect a wrong branch and keep an editable construction.

name: horologium
description: Explore 13 calendars, ancient planets checked against DE441, and local sunrise and sunset; marginal polar events stay unresolved.

study.finding: 74 sites across 2026: 90 false solar crossings removed; marginal polar events withheld. Terrain and weather remain outside the model.

name: gnomon
description: Design horizontal, wall, equatorial and analemmatic sundials; preview either equatorial face and print a full-scale kit with a shared mirrored cut.

study.finding: Pole-facing and opposite faces share one cut; polar azimuth corrected. Native checks: 1,383 SVG rays, 3,521 PDF ray copies. Physical assembly unverified.

name: planisphere
description: Build a printable star wheel for either hemisphere, check southern sky orientation, and compare stellar epochs from 3000 BCE to 3000 CE.

study.finding: 2,668 printable star positions: 1,164 mirrored positions corrected against independent outward-view geometry. Physical printing remains unverified.

name: tonemirror
description: Practice with recorded Mandarin; preserve unvoiced gaps and choose separate stereo channels and a pitch search floor for each voice.

study.finding: 580 recordings: 40 Hz improves reference agreement below 60 Hz but adds false voicing. Separate voice floors; default 60 Hz. Pronunciation untested.

name: errorbars
description: Compare LLM evals on recorded task intersections, account for repository clusters, and inspect missing outcomes before ranking.

study.finding: A public SWE-bench file records 441/500 tasks. Removing 59 invented failures changes paired-task p from 0.000060 to 0.644; official score unchanged.

name: mergeglass
description: Source audit: saved LoRA/DoRA and BF16 merges, Conv1D, embedding adapters, scaled B bias and Qwen3 MoE expert parameters; full saved heads, learned row norms and partial observations without loading a model.

study.finding: 44 native MoE saves: omitted experts give gain 0; wrong B order changes a zero-reference expert. Saved-head and bias controls stay replayable.

name: contextscope
description: Diagnose prompt-cache misses from captured Anthropic/OpenAI requests; MCP tools, media and stored history keep unresolved token counts explicit.

study.finding: MCP URLs do not reveal model-visible tools: 11 SDK workflows now keep token/cache totals unknown; two local-tool controls retain known totals.

name: fieldproof
description: Review scanned receipt PDFs locally, inspect native and OCR words beside page images, and keep evidence provenance through corrections, exports and archived reviews.

study.finding: Source upgrade: a scanned CORD receipt opens locally; 12 API cases retain OCR provenance and eight archives. Hosted example is precomputed.

name: mcplint
description: Capture and compare actual MCP tool contracts: enum/type contradictions, dependency drift, token estimates, descriptions and hidden-instruction heuristics.

study.finding: Four native enum/type contradictions across three SVGverseAI tools; empty calls stay valid. Retained 25,799-tool audits preserve previous findings.

name: veil
description: Mask detected personal data and credentials in native HAR exports and ordinary URLs; keep a local vault and restore exact values across reply chunks.

study.finding: 16,082 held-out phone numbers with a +: masking rose from 53.9% to 99.3%. International numbers without + remain a detection gap.

name: tracelens
description: Open local OTLP or Jaeger traces, including Zstandard Collector JSON/protobuf; follow span evidence, compare runs and reconcile recorded token costs.

study.finding: Native Collector exports: all 5,001 SDK spans survive compressed imports offline. Damaged streams refuse; this is a controlled local workload.

name: trainspotter
description: Source/live workbench: native binary .wandb logs, quoted W&B CSV and MLflow histories, typed gaps, explicit model/dataset scopes, and offline charts with source/axis context.

study.finding: Native W&B: 400 history packets match independent SDK/Go readers; text NaN remains a gap while observed overflow stays divergence.

name: ghostchars
description: See the characters you can't: catch Trojan Source bidi tricks, invisible and lookalike Unicode, and ASCII smuggling in code and LLM prompts.

study.finding: Source upgrade: 31 JavaScript controls with escaped identifiers expose 124 missed confusable spans; parsing checks names without resolving scope.

name: logdelta
description: Diff logs by meaning, not by bytes: masks variables, mines templates, and shows what's new in the failing run.

study.finding: 264 failed Kubernetes builds: excerpts show the recorded reason in 212/239 eligible cases, at 40.5 median lines. The rule was tuned on these logs.

name: flakemap
description: Read JUnit, native NUnit XML or .NET TRX histories. Inspect distinct fixtures, retry evidence and uncertain outcomes in a ranked CI report.

study.finding: 44,724 native NUnit case records from unchanged NodaTime and Math.NET suites match an independent identity/outcome oracle.

name: stutterscope
description: Open native CapFrameX JSON or PresentMon 2.6 CSV, select a recording, and inspect frame-time gaps with CPU, GPU and latency source evidence.

study.finding: Native PresentMon 2.6: 174 filtered frames retain CPU/GPU and latency; 83 clock gaps leave 90 observed pacing pairs.

name: splitscope
description: Compare completed attempts and reset segments by count or elapsed attempt time; inspect linked LiveSplit attempts and unavailable clocks in your browser.

study.finding: Re-Loaded: 10 Desert resets total 3:56; four Monestary resets total 48:18. Elapsed clocks include pauses; missing and overlapping clocks stay explicit.

name: am-i-unlucky
description: Plan explicit drop batches from the next weekly reset; inspect community-logged Genshin pity rates and collection odds, and share luck cards with ties visible.

study.finding: Weekly 50% attempt starting on day 2: 9-day mean; day 7: 14 days. Checked against 134 rational models; calendar-time forecasts omitted.
